script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

Title: FRESH STARTS

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

ANNE, 40s, wears a frown as she pours herself a cup of coffee. Her eyes dart to the framed photo of herself in a suit on her kitchen counter. She's dressed casually in jeans and a t-shirt today. She looks at it longingly.

ANNE
(to herself)
Twelve years...

INT. ANNE'S HOME OFFICE - DAY

Anne sits in her home office, staring at her computer screen. Her eyes are heavy and filled with doubt as she types and deletes lines of code. Her phone rings, and she picks up.

ANNE
(on phone)
Yes, I understand. But... I need time to consider this.

INT. LIVING ROOM - AFTERNOON

Anne sits on the couch, her laptop open on her legs. Her husband, MIKE, enters the room, carrying their children's homework.

MIKE
(placing the papers on the coffee table)
How's it going?

ANNE
(sighs)
I'm not sure. I've been offered a promotion at work. But it means moving to New York.

MIKE
(surprised)
Really? Why would they offer you a promotion if you're not sure?

ANNE
(shrugs)
I don't know. I've been feeling disconnected from my job lately. I need a change.

MIKE
(concerned)
But what about us? And the kids?

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Anne stands at the sink, washing the dinner dishes. She looks out the window to see her children playing in the yard.

ANNE
(to herself)
I need to figure this out. For them.

INT. ANNE'S HOME OFFICE - NIGHT

Anne sits at her computer, searching for information on New York. She comes across an article about a local community center that offers classes and workshops for career transitions.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

Anne attends her first workshop. She meets JANET, a woman her age who's going through a similar transition.

JANET
(smiling)
Nice to meet you. I'm Janet. I used to work in marketing, just like you. But I left my job to start my own business.

ANNE
(intrigued)
Really? What kind of business?

JANET
(proudly)
I make organic skincare products. It's been a challenge, but it's also been incredibly rewarding.

ANNE
(inspired)
That's amazing. I've been feeling disconnected from my job for a while now. I need a change.

JANET
(encouragingly)
You can do it, Anne. It won't be easy, but it will be worth it.

INT. ANNE'S HOME OFFICE - NIGHT

Anne sits at her computer, typing away at her new business plan. She smiles as she reads through her ideas.

ANNE
(to herself)
I can do this.

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

Anne makes breakfast for her family. She serves them each a plate and sits down to join them.

MIKE
(looking at her thoughtfully)
You seem happier lately.

ANNE
(smiling)
I am. I've decided to leave my job and start my own business.

MIKE
(proud of her)
That's great, Anne. I'll support you every step of the way.

ANNE
(grateful)
Thank you. I couldn't do it without you.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

Anne attends a business planning workshop. She presents her ideas to a group of mentors and receives valuable feedback.

MENTOR
(approvingly)
Anne, this is a fantastic business idea. You have a real opportunity here.

ANNE
(excited)
Thank you. I can't wait to get started.

INT. ANNE'S HOME OFFICE - NIGHT

Anne works late into the night, finalizing her business plan. She looks up from her computer and smiles, knowing that she's finally found her fresh start.

THE END.
